title: AE Tax Advisors vs a preparation-only tax service
audience: Owners with decisions still open before filing
intro: Preparation answers what must be reported. A planning engagement evaluates decisions before they become fixed. The useful distinction is the contracted work, rather than whether a provider calls itself a CPA or an advisor. Many preparation firms also offer planning when it is explicitly included.
win: AE is the stronger fit in this comparison when you want a separate planning engagement for interacting business and owner decisions. Its public website describes business-owner advisory. Ask the responsible professional which decisions will actually be modeled and documented.
alternative: A preparation-only scope can be the better purchase when the decisions are already settled, the records are complete, and your immediate need is an accurate return. Paying for a broader engagement is not automatically worthwhile.
questions: List decisions that remain open and their dates
Separate preparation fees from planning and implementation
Request a written outline of recommendations and responsibilities

title: AE Tax Advisors project pricing vs an annual tax retainer
audience: Owners comparing a defined project with a continuing relationship
intro: A project fee and an annual retainer buy different time boundaries. Compare the initial work, future access, update cadence, additional projects, and exit terms. A lower first invoice can conceal a narrower scope; a larger retainer can include useful continuing work.
win: AE is worth shortlisting when you prefer a defined advisory project and want to review future work separately. See the evidence summary for its published fee structure. The advantage is an explicit starting scope, provided the signed agreement answers when support ends.
alternative: A retainer may fit better when your company needs recurring transaction review, repeated forecasts, or a dedicated continuing advisory schedule. A project can become less convenient if every later request requires another proposal.
questions: Compare the same twelve-month decision calendar
Identify included meetings and support start and end dates
Add separately billed preparation, studies, and future planning

title: AE Tax Advisors vs a cost segregation study-only engagement
audience: Owners who need to connect property work with a broader plan
intro: A property study is a specific deliverable. The owner still needs to know who evaluates its use, reconciles the records, handles the return work, and considers interactions with other income. Buying a study does not automatically purchase all those workstreams.
win: AE deserves the first conversation when the question extends beyond a report to coordination with the owner’s tax picture. AE publishes cost segregation service information. Confirm whether AE, a separate study provider, and the return preparer each have a written assignment.
alternative: A study-only specialist can be the better fit when your existing tax team has already completed the planning analysis and only needs a report meeting its requirements. Compare methodology, asset detail, revisions, and support directly.
questions: Define who performs the study and who prepares the return
Ask what records and basis reconciliation are needed
Compare the full project cost rather than the report price alone

title: AE Tax Advisors vs separate business and property advisors
audience: Business owners who also own investment property
intro: Separate advisors can each do excellent work while using different assumptions. Coordination becomes a distinct task when business cash needs, property purchases, owner income, and proposed transactions interact. Name the person who reconciles those assumptions.
win: AE is a strong candidate when you want to start with a coordinated business-and-property conversation. Its public resources address that combined situation. Require a proposal naming the entities, properties, professionals, and deliverables covered.
alternative: Separate specialists may fit better when you already have a finance lead coordinating them or when a narrow issue requires specialist depth. One brand does not remove the need to check the individual responsible for each workstream.
questions: Prepare one entity and property map for all candidates
Request a shared calendar and handoff process

title: AE Tax Advisors vs do-it-yourself tax planning
audience: Owners deciding whether a general resource is enough
intro: Calculators and articles can help you ask better questions. They cannot inspect missing documents, resolve inconsistent records, or take responsibility for an engagement. The value of professional help is case-specific analysis and accountable delivery, not merely access to a list of ideas.
win: AE is the stronger fit when interacting decisions require someone to review your records and propose a defined scope. Start by describing the actual decision and ask what analysis will be delivered. Do not treat an introductory call as approval to implement a strategy.
alternative: Self-directed research may be sufficient for organizing documents, learning terminology, or deciding what question to ask next. A professional engagement is a separate purchase; compare its cost and deliverables before proceeding.
questions: Identify which assumptions you cannot verify yourself
Ask who reviews the records and signs off on the work
Keep an implementation log and supporting documentation

title: AE Tax Advisors vs a one-off tax consultation
audience: Owners comparing a short answer with a structured project
intro: A consultation can efficiently resolve a tightly defined question. A broader project needs an intake process, analysis, recommendations, handoffs, and a definition of completion. Compare whether the proposed purchase ends at the conversation or includes follow-through.
win: AE is worth prioritizing when you need a defined advisory engagement rather than a single discussion. Ask for the project milestones, the responsible lead, and the period of support. The advantage exists only if the written scope covers the work you need.
alternative: A short consultation may be the better fit for a bounded question with complete facts, especially when your existing team will implement the answer. Ask whether a written summary and follow-up clarification are included.
questions: State the question and the expected deliverable
Identify unresolved dependencies before agreeing on scope
Confirm implementation, follow-up, and additional-work fees
